symptom: In an `if` without `else` whose true branch was placed on the merge's line with @position, the edge from the branch's last activity into the closing merge entered the merge at the bottom and looped under it; the decision's @anchor changed only the false edge, so 'true runs right into the merge, false drops below and comes up into it' could not be written.
cause: The branch-tail -> merge edge was built with newUpwardFlow, which hard-codes right -> bottom: correct for a branch in mxcli's default lane below, wrong for one moved onto the merge's line. A merge has no statement, so DESCRIBE writes no `to:` for that edge and nothing can override it.
fix: The edge's destination side comes from geometry (mergeEntrySide -> mergeSideFor): bottom for a branch below the merge, left on its line, top above. Same for the else branch of an if/else.
insight: An edge whose end side the description never writes is decided by the builder alone, so the builder has to read it from geometry, not from the default layout: a hard-coded side is only right while nothing is moved. mergeSideFor already did this for CASE branches. Verified on 11.14.0: the issue's repro stores log -> merge right -> left and the false edge bottom -> bottom, describe matches the script, mx check 0 errors.
test: mdl/executor/merge_entry_side_2593_test.go (two repro variants plus the default-lane control); failed before (right -> bottom)
